newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Speculation up on Callaway.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Speculation up on Callaway.

text.p: Speculation in Callaway Golf Co was on the rise Monday, with options investors playing both sides, traders said.
"There's been a lot of public interest in the Feb 30 and 35 calls over the last four or five days," an options trader in Chicago said.
"Both covered writers and speculators (are) coming in on the long side trying to buy them," he said.
A trader in New York noted that the Investment Research Institute had recommended buying the February 30 calls, which helped boost interest in the options.
"We sent out a recommendation on Friday," Joseph Sunderman, a research analyst at the Cincinnati-based firm said. "But there was volume before that.
"We saw the volume and we saw the call premiums priced pretty high," Sunderman explained. "We saw the shares moving higher and thought that was possibly smart money."
He said the stock's chart pattern also contributed to the recommendation, as the stock moved above its 200-day moving average on Friday.
Callaway's quarterly earnings are due out later this week.

Shares of the golf club maker rallied 1-1/2 points to 31-3/8 on Friday, cracking its 200-day moving average, which came into play at 30-5/8. The stock was up another 5/8 at 32 in late trading Monday after reaching 32-3/8 intraday.
A week ago, an institutional investor shorted about 4,100 of the Callaway February 30 calls, and traders said that activity drew others into the strategy.

On Monday, the February 35 call was most active, with a total of 1,345 contracts changing hands. The option had open interest of 2,892 through Friday. The February 30 call traded more than 800 contracts. Its open interest was 12,080.
Among Callaway puts, the August 30 and 35 were most active, with volume of 350 and 340, respectively.
The trader in Chicago said despite the increased speculation, volatilities in the options held steady.
"Volatilities came in a little bit going into last Thursday and Friday, but with the move on Friday, front month volatility has creeped up," he said.
He said volatilities were in the mid-40 region.
Besides this week's earnings, a golf/recreation show is scheduled for the end of the week, traders said.
